description: Get the state of the fleet at a glance: host counts, open alerts, hosts over a limit, the top 5 hosts by CPU, memory and disk, and the alerts and notifications of the last 24 hours.
name: fleet_summary
title: Fleet summary

description: List the hosts of the fleet with the latest CPU (percent), memory and disk (ratio 0 to 1), load and network (bytes each second). Offline hosts have no values.

limit.description: most hosts to return, 1 to 200. Default 50.

sort.description: order of the hosts, highest first: cpu, mem, disk or net. Default cpu.

name: list_hosts
title: List hosts

description: Get one host: its latest values, facts (OS, kernel, cores, memory, uptime), open alerts and the effective limits with their source (org or host).
name: get_host
title: Get host

description: Get the history of metrics of one host, of many hosts or of a tag: min, avg, max, last and a capped list of points for each metric. Any history metric works (see reference). With compare, each metric also has the window before the range and the change of the average. The plan can shorten the range (clamped).

compare.description: also read the window of the same length before the range. Each series then has previous and change_avg, and the biggest change comes first.

from.description: start of the range in RFC 3339. Use it with to, instead of range.

host.description: one host, by ID or name. Give one of host, hosts or tag.

hosts.description: at most 50 hosts, by ID or name

metrics.description: history metrics to read: cpu, mem, net_rx, net_tx, disk_read, disk_write, load_1, load (the same as load_1), procs, disk, inodes, zombies, pids, files, psi_cpu, psi_mem, psi_mem_full, psi_io, psi_io_full and mem_pressure. At most 16 for one host and 8 for many hosts. Default cpu. Call reference with topic metrics for the units.

range.description: span up to now, 15m to 365d (30d for many hosts), for example 1h, 24h or 7d. Default 1h. Do not use with from.

resolution.description: auto, raw, 1m, 5m or 1h. Default auto. The server raises the step to keep at most 300 points.

tag.description: all hosts with this tag, at most 50

to.description: end of the range in RFC 3339. Default now.

name: host_metrics
title: Host metrics

description: Get the top processes of one host, or of the fleet, by CPU, memory or disk I/O over a range. With at and a host, get the processes at one time, with PID, user and state. Each process has its start time and run time where known.

at.description: one point in time instead of a range: RFC 3339, now or now-<span>, for example now-2h. Needs host. Gives PID, user and state for a time in the last hour.

by.description: order: cpu (average CPU), mem (peak memory) or io (average disk I/O). Default cpu.

from.description: start of the range in RFC 3339. Use it with to, instead of range.

host.description: host ID or name. Empty means the whole fleet.

limit.description: most processes to return, 1 to 50. Default 20.

range.description: span up to now, 15m to 365d, for example 1h, 24h or 7d. Default 1h. Do not use with from or at.

to.description: end of the range in RFC 3339. Default now.

name: top_processes
title: Top processes

description: Get the history of one process of a host: CPU, memory and disk I/O points, the stats of the range, the facts (PID, user, ports) and the start time. The process is a key from top_processes or a name.

from.description: start of the range in RFC 3339. Use it with to, instead of range.

process.description: the key of a process from top_processes, or a process name. A name that has more than one command gives an error with the keys.

range.description: span up to now, 15m to 365d, for example 1h, 24h or 7d. Default 1h. Do not use with from.

to.description: end of the range in RFC 3339. Default now.

name: process_history
title: Process history

description: List the alerts of the fleet or of one host: the open alerts by default, or the alerts of a range. Filter by state, kind, severity and text. Each alert has its severity, state, value, peak, start and end. The result also has the counts of each state.

from.description: start of the range in RFC 3339. Use it with to, instead of range.

host.description: host ID or name. Empty means the whole fleet.

kind.description: keep these kinds: cpu, mem, disk, health, long (long-running process) or nodata

limit.description: most alerts to return, 1 to 100. Default 50.

q.description: text to find in the host name, the metric and the process name or command

range.description: span up to now, for example 24h or 7d. Alerts that overlap the range count. At most 90d. Default 7d. Do not use with from.

sort.description: sev (default), start, peak, duration, title, host, kind or state. The number sorts give the highest first. The text sorts give A to Z.

state.description: open (not resolved, default), action (open, not acked, not snoozed), resolved or all

tint.description: keep these severities (the worst level of the alert): critical or warn

to.description: end of the range in RFC 3339. Default now.

name: alerts
title: List alerts

description: Get one alert: its timeline (opened, changed, notified, acked, snoozed, recovered), the limits that it had, the rule that applies to its host now and the number of notifications.

alert_id.description: alert ID, from the alerts tool

name: get_alert
title: Get alert

description: Get the alert rules of the organization, or of one host: limits, sustain times, notify levels, muted metrics, the long-process rule and the notification switches. For a host, also the overrides and the effective rules with the source (org or host) of each.

host.description: host ID or name. Empty gives the rules of the organization only.

name: host_rules
title: Host rules

description: Get the use of each disk mount of one host and the change over a range.

range.description: span up to now, 15m to 365d, for example 24h or 7d. Default 24h.

name: disks
title: Disk use

description: Get the disk scans of one host: the newest 5 jobs and, for the newest finished scan or a job_id, the file system, the 20 largest entries and the cleanup recommendations.

job_id.description: scan job ID, from an earlier call. Default: the newest finished scan.

name: disk_scans
title: Disk scans

description: Get the statistics of the alerts of a range: the totals, the notifications (and the ones sent by email), the alerts and notifications by host, kind, rule and channel, the metrics that flap (many short alerts) and the alert starts over time. Use it first to find why alerts came.

from.description: start of the range in RFC 3339. Use it with to, instead of range.

host.description: host ID or name. Empty means the whole fleet.

kind.description: keep these kinds: cpu, mem, disk, health, long (long-running process) or nodata

range.description: span up to now, for example 24h or 7d. Alerts that overlap the range count. At most 90d. Default 7d. Do not use with from.

to.description: end of the range in RFC 3339. Default now.

top.description: length of the top lists (hosts, rules, flapping), 1 to 20. Default 10.

name: alert_stats
title: Alert statistics

description: Find the level shifts of one metric of one host over a range, such as a jump of CPU use. For the largest shift, get the processes that rose or fell (CPU, memory or disk I/O, by metric) and the alerts of the host that started around it. Use it to find why a metric changed.

from.description: start of the range in RFC 3339. Use it with to, instead of range.

metric.description: history metric to explain, for example cpu or mem. Call reference with topic metrics for the names and units.

range.description: span up to now, 15m to 365d, for example 6h or 24h. Default 24h. Do not use with from.

to.description: end of the range in RFC 3339. Default now.

name: explain_change
title: Explain a metric change

description: Get the facts behind a metric, a rule or a plan limit. Topics: metrics, thresholds, alerts, long_process, history and plan.

topic.description: one of: metrics, thresholds, alerts, long_process, history, plan

name: reference
title: Reference facts

description: Get the organization, the plan, the history limit and the sign-in (token kind and role) of this connection.
name: whoami
title: Who am I
